examples.en: The kids made glasses out of red cellophane paper.

examples.ko: 셀로판지를 눈앞에 대면 세상이 다른 색으로 보여요.
examples.en: If you hold cellophane paper in front of your eyes, the world looks a different color.

examples.ko: 이 셀로판지는 너무 얇아서 자꾸 찢어져요.
examples.en: This cellophane paper is so thin that it keeps tearing.

examples.ko: 창문에 분홍 셀로판지를 붙이니 방이 따뜻해 보여요.
examples.en: With pink cellophane paper on the window, the room looks warm.

examples.ko: 선물을 투명한 셀로판지에 싸고 리본을 묶었어요.
examples.en: I wrapped the gift in clear cellophane paper and tied a ribbon.

examples.ko: 셀로판지 한 장만 빌려줄 수 있어요?
examples.en: Could you lend me just one sheet of cellophane paper?

explain: 얇고 빛이 비치는 포장·공작 재료예요. 색깔 셀로판지를 눈이나 손전등에 대고 노는 만들기 수업에 자주 나와요. 줄여서 '셀로판'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is a thin, see-through material used for wrapping and crafts. Colored sheets often appear in craft classes, held over eyes or flashlights. It is also shortened to '셀로판'.

examples.en: We started our married life in a cramped rented room.

examples.ko: 십 년 넘게 셋방살이를 하다가 드디어 집을 샀어요.
examples.en: After renting a room for over ten years, I finally bought a house.

examples.ko: 셋방살이가 설움이 많다고 할머니가 자주 말씀하셨어요.
examples.en: Grandmother often said that living in a rented room brings a lot of hardship.

examples.ko: 셋방살이 신세를 벗어나는 게 우리 부모님의 꿈이었어요.
examples.en: Getting out of life in a rented room was my parents' dream.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 셋방살이할 때는 화장실을 같이 썼어요.
examples.en: When we rented a room in my childhood, we shared the bathroom.

examples.ko: 주인집 눈치를 보며 셋방살이하는 게 힘들었어요.
examples.en: It was hard living in a rented room, watching the landlord's mood.

explain: 요즘은 '세 들어 살다'가 더 자연스럽고, '셋방살이'는 어렵던 시절 이야기나 회상에서 많이 나와요. 방 한 칸을 빌려 쓰는 느낌이 강해서, 집 전체를 빌리는 경우와는 조금 달라요.
explain_en: Today '세 들어 살다' sounds more natural, while '셋방살이' often shows up in stories about hard times or in recollections. It carries the feeling of renting a single room, so it differs a bit from renting a whole home.

examples.ko: 쓰레기 소각장이 우리 동네에 생긴다고 해서 걱정이에요.
examples.en: I'm worried because they say a waste incineration plant is going to be built in our neighborhood.

examples.ko: 소각장에서 나오는 열로 근처 아파트에 난방을 해요.
examples.en: They heat nearby apartments with the heat from the incineration plant.
The residents are opposing the construction of the incineration plant.

examples.ko: 소각장은 매연 때문에 늘 논란이 돼요.
examples.en: Incineration plants are always controversial because of the smoke.
A truck carrying waste to the incineration plant is passing by.

examples.ko: 공장 옆 소각장 때문에 냄새가 난다는 민원이 많아요.
examples.en: There are many complaints that the incineration plant next to the factory causes a smell.

explain: 쓰레기를 태워서 처리하는 곳이고, 땅에 묻어서 처리하는 곳은 '매립지'라고 해요. 뉴스에서는 '소각장 건설 반대'처럼 주민 갈등 이야기에 자주 나와요.
explain_en: This is a place that disposes of trash by burning it, while a place that buries trash is called '매립지'. In the news it often appears in stories about resident conflicts, such as opposition to building an incineration plant.

examples.en: I got a doctor's note from the hospital and submitted it to my company.
You need a referral note to go to a large hospital.
Where do I get the doctor's note issued?

examples.ko: 소견서에 제 상태가 자세히 적혀 있었어요.
examples.en: My condition was written in detail in the note.

examples.ko: 소견서 한 장 때문에 병원을 두 번 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to the hospital twice just for one doctor's note.
Can I apply for insurance with this note?

explain: 진단서가 병명을 공식적으로 증명하는 서류라면, 소견서는 의사의 의견을 적은 글이에요. 다른 병원으로 갈 때 받는 서류는 '진료의뢰서'라고도 해요. 보통 '소견서를 받다/떼다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: If a 진단서 is an official document certifying a diagnosis, a 소견서 is a written statement of the doctor's opinion. A document for moving to another hospital is also called '진료의뢰서'. People usually say '소견서를 받다' or '소견서를 떼다'.

examples.en: Friends are whispering something at the back of the classroom.
In the library, you have to talk in whispers.
The child whispered into my ear.
Why are you two still whispering?
Please don't whisper in the movie theater.
I can hear all the whispering behind me.

explain: '소곤거리다'와 같은 말이고, 남이 듣지 않도록 작은 목소리로 이야기하는 모습에 써요. '속삭이다'는 귀에 대고 다정하게 말하는 느낌이 더 있어요. '소곤소곤'처럼 부사로도 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is the same as '소곤거리다' and describes talking in a small voice so others will not hear. '속삭이다' has more of a tender feel, like speaking right into someone's ear. It is also often used as the adverb '소곤소곤'.

examples.en: The two keep whispering in the corner.
I can hear the children whispering.
We were whispering during class and got caught by the teacher.
I couldn't sleep because I was whispering all night.
What were you two whispering about like that?
Don't whisper, speak up.

explain: 일상에서는 '소곤소곤 말해요'처럼 부사로 쓰는 경우가 더 자연스러워요. 같은 느낌의 동사로 '소곤거리다', '소곤대다'도 있어요. 작은 소리로 둘이 이야기하는 장면에 어울려요.
explain_en: In daily speech, using it as an adverb, as in '소곤소곤 말해요', sounds more natural. The verbs '소곤거리다' and '소곤대다' carry the same feel. It suits scenes where two people talk quietly together.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 친구들과 소꿉을 가지고 놀았어요.
examples.en: As a child, I played with toys for playing house with my friends.

examples.ko: 소꿉으로 밥상을 차리는 게 제일 재미있었어요.
examples.en: Setting the table with the toy dishes was the most fun.

examples.ko: 마당에서 소꿉질을 하던 아이들이 집으로 들어갔어요.
examples.en: The children who were playing house in the yard went inside.

examples.ko: 딸이 소꿉놀이를 하자고 해서 같이 놀았어요.
examples.en: My daughter asked to play house, so I played with her.
I was happy to meet my childhood friend after a long time.

examples.ko: 아이가 소꿉이 마음에 드는지 하루 종일 놀아요.
examples.en: The child must like the toy set, as she plays with it all day.

explain: 혼자 쓰기보다 '소꿉놀이', '소꿉장난', '소꿉친구'처럼 다른 말과 붙여서 많이 써요. '소꿉친구'는 어릴 때부터 같이 놀며 큰 친구를 말해서 '어릴 적 친구'보다 정겨운 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is usually used attached to other words, as in '소꿉놀이', '소꿉장난' and '소꿉친구', rather than alone. '소꿉친구' means a friend you grew up playing with, and it feels warmer than '어릴 적 친구'.

examples.en: During boyhood, you grow a lot taller all of a sudden.
He said he spent a poor boyhood.

examples.ko: 소년기의 경험이 그 사람의 성격을 만들었어요.
examples.en: His experiences in boyhood shaped his personality.

examples.ko: 소년기가 끝나 갈 때쯤 이사를 했어요.
examples.en: We moved around the time his boyhood was coming to an end.

examples.ko: 소년기 때 읽은 책이 아직도 기억나요.
examples.en: I still remember the books I read in my boyhood.
I lived in the same neighborhood from boyhood to young adulthood.

explain: '유년기, 소년기, 청년기'처럼 인생 단계를 나열할 때 써요. '소년'이 남자아이를 가리켜서 보통 남자의 어린 시절 이야기에 쓰고, 성별과 상관없이 말할 때는 '청소년기'가 더 넓게 쓰여요.
explain_en: It is used when listing life stages, as in '유년기, 소년기, 청년기'. Since '소년' refers to a boy, it is mostly used for a boy's early years, and '청소년기' is broader when gender does not matter.

examples.en: The fruit came out piled attractively on the plate.

examples.ko: 소담한 한 상을 차려 주셔서 감사해요.
examples.en: Thank you for setting such a lovely, generous table.

examples.ko: 꽃이 소담해서 보기만 해도 기분이 좋아요.
examples.en: The flowers are so full and lovely that just looking at them cheers me up.
This is a pleasant, neat Korean restaurant.

examples.ko: 엄마가 싸 주신 도시락은 작지만 소담했어요.
examples.en: The lunchbox Mom packed was small but looked lovely and full.
The table isn't lavish, but I prepared it with care.

explain: 음식, 꽃, 열매처럼 모양이 탐스럽고 보기 좋을 때 써요. '푸짐하다'가 양이 많은 데 초점이라면 '소담하다'는 보기 좋게 넉넉한 느낌이 있어요. 대화보다는 식당 소개나 글에서 더 어울려요.
explain_en: It is used when food, flowers or fruit look full and pleasing. While '푸짐하다' focuses on large quantity, '소담하다' adds a pleasant, generous look. It fits restaurant introductions and writing better than casual talk.

examples.en: We make the stage props for the play ourselves.

examples.ko: 소도구 담당을 맡은 친구가 바빠 보여요.
examples.en: The friend in charge of props looks busy.

examples.ko: 무대에 필요한 소도구를 미리 준비해 두세요.
examples.en: Please prepare the props needed for the stage in advance.

examples.ko: 이 사진관에는 촬영용 소도구가 아주 많아요.
examples.en: This photo studio has a lot of props for shoots.

examples.ko: 작은 소도구도 연기에 큰 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: Even a small prop is a big help to acting.
We decided to use a hat and a cane as props.

explain: 연극, 영화, 사진 촬영에서 배우가 들거나 쓰는 작은 물건을 말해요. 무대 배경처럼 큰 것은 '대도구'라고 해요. 비슷한 말로 '소품'이 있어요.
explain_en: It refers to small items actors hold or use in plays, films and photo shoots. Large things such as stage backdrops are called '대도구'. A similar word is '소품'.

examples.ko: 열 시에 소등하니까 그 전에 씻으세요.
examples.en: The lights go out at ten, so wash up before then.

examples.ko: 기숙사는 밤 열한 시에 소등이 돼요.
examples.en: The dormitory lights go out at eleven at night.
When lights-out time came, the room got dark.

examples.ko: 행사 때 모두 함께 소등하기로 했어요.
examples.en: We decided to turn off all the lights together during the event.

examples.ko: 소등한 뒤에도 잠이 안 와서 뒤척였어요.
examples.en: Even after the lights went out, I couldn't sleep and tossed and turned.

examples.ko: 방 소등을 깜빡해서 밤새 불이 켜져 있었어요.
examples.en: I forgot to turn off the room light, so it stayed on all night.

explain: 반대말은 불을 켜는 '점등'이에요. 일상에서는 '불 끄다'라고 하고, '소등'은 기숙사, 극장, 행사 안내처럼 여러 사람이 함께 지내는 곳의 방송이나 공지에서 많이 나와요.
explain_en: Its opposite is '점등', turning lights on. In daily life people say '불 끄다', while '소등' appears in announcements and notices in places where many people stay together, such as dormitories, theaters and events.

examples.ko: 아기가 엄마 품에서 소르르 잠이 들었어요.
examples.en: The baby drifted off to sleep in her mother's arms.
I'm sleepy and my eyes are slowly closing.
The ribbon came undone smoothly and the gift opened.
The ice melted away gently in the warm sunshine.
The sand slipped softly through my fingers.
The hem of the skirt slid down softly.

explain: '잠들다, 졸리다, 풀리다, 녹다' 같은 말과 함께 써요. 가볍고 부드럽게 일어나는 일을 그릴 때 어울려요. 같은 뜻의 '스르르'가 큰말이라서, '소르르'는 조금 더 작고 가벼운 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It goes with words like '잠들다', '졸리다', '풀리다' and '녹다', and fits things that happen lightly and gently. '스르르' is the larger-sounding counterpart, so '소르르' feels a little smaller and lighter.

examples.ko: 소매상은 도매상에게서 물건을 사 와서 팔아요.
examples.en: Retailers buy goods from wholesalers and sell them.
My parents run a small retail shop.
Retailers are pushing back against the price increase.
I tend to buy fruit from a local retailer.

examples.ko: 소매상 몇 곳에 전화해서 가격을 비교했어요.
examples.en: I called a few retailers and compared prices.
The wholesaler discussed terms of trade with the retailer.

explain: '도매상'의 반대말로, 물건을 소비자에게 직접 파는 상인이나 가게를 말해요. 가게 자체는 '소매점', 그런 업종은 '소매업'이라고 해서 셋이 짝을 이뤄요.
explain_en: It is the opposite of '도매상' and refers to a merchant or shop that sells directly to consumers. The shop itself is '소매점' and the line of business is '소매업', so the three words form a set.

examples.en: Convenience stores and supermarkets are typical retail businesses.

examples.ko: 요즘 소매업은 온라인 쇼핑 때문에 경쟁이 심해요.
examples.en: Retail these days is highly competitive because of online shopping.

examples.ko: 삼촌은 소매업에 종사하며 옷 가게를 운영해요.
examples.en: My uncle works in retail and runs a clothing store.

examples.ko: 소매업에서 일하려면 손님 응대를 잘해야 해요.
examples.en: To work in retail, you need to be good at serving customers.
They say retail sales fell compared with last month.
I switched my business from wholesale to retail.

explain: '도매업'과 짝이 되는 말이에요. 뉴스에서는 '소매업 매출'처럼 경제 이야기에 자주 나오고, 하는 일을 말할 때는 '소매업에 종사하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It pairs with '도매업' (wholesale). In the news it often appears in economic stories, as in '소매업 매출', and for one's line of work you say '소매업에 종사하다'.

examples.ko: 도매 시장에서는 소매점보다 훨씬 싼 값에 물건을 살 수 있어요.
examples.en: At a wholesale market you can buy goods at a much cheaper price than at retail stores.
This brand is sold at retail stores nationwide.

examples.ko: 동네 소매점이 대형 마트 때문에 문을 닫았어요.
examples.en: The local retail shop closed because of the big supermarket.

examples.ko: 소매점을 열려면 먼저 위치부터 정해야 해요.
examples.en: To open a retail store, you first have to decide the location.
Prices differ a little from one retail store to another.

examples.ko: 우리 가게는 도매도 하고 소매점도 같이 해요.
examples.en: Our business does wholesale and runs a retail store as well.

explain: 일상에서는 그냥 '가게'나 '상점'이라고 하고, '소매점'은 도매와 비교하거나 유통 이야기를 할 때 써요. 소비자에게 직접 파는 곳이라는 점이 도매 시장과 다른 점이에요.
explain_en: In daily life people simply say '가게' or '상점', and '소매점' is used when contrasting with wholesale or talking about distribution. What sets it apart from a wholesale market is that it sells directly to consumers.

examples.en: The child grabbed my sleeve and wouldn't let go.
I wiped my tears away with my sleeve.
The sleeve of the hanbok fluttered in the wind.
Kimchi broth got on my sleeve.
The end of the sleeve was frayed, so I took it to be repaired.
The clothes are big, so the sleeves hang down over the backs of my hands.

explain: '소매'가 가장 일상적인 말이고, '소맷자락'은 늘어진 소매 부분을 느낌 있게 말할 때 써요. 한복이나 이야기 속 장면에서 잘 어울려요. 소매의 끝부분만 가리킬 때는 '소매 끝'이라고 해도 돼요.
explain_en: '소매' is the everyday word, while '소맷자락' describes the hanging part of a sleeve with more feeling. It suits hanbok and story scenes. To point only to the end of a sleeve, you can also say '소매 끝'.

examples.ko: 두 회사의 가격 경쟁은 소모전이 되고 말았어요.
examples.en: The price competition between the two companies turned into a war of attrition.

examples.ko: 이런 소모전은 빨리 끝내는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's better to end this kind of draining fight quickly.

examples.ko: 괜한 소모전을 벌이지 말고 대화로 풀어요.
examples.en: Let's not start a pointless fight and settle it by talking.

examples.ko: 소모전으로 번진 싸움에서는 둘 다 손해를 봐요.
examples.en: In a fight that turns into a war of attrition, both sides lose.

examples.ko: 소모전 끝에 양쪽 모두 지쳐 버렸어요.
examples.en: After the long drawn-out fight, both sides were exhausted.
The debate is dragging on like a war of attrition.

explain: 전쟁뿐 아니라 회사 경쟁, 논쟁, 다툼처럼 힘과 시간만 쓰고 얻는 것은 별로 없는 싸움을 비유할 때도 많이 써요. '소모전을 벌이다', '소모전으로 치닫다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: Beyond actual wars, it is often used figuratively for company rivalry, debates and quarrels that use up energy and time with little gain. People say '소모전을 벌이다' or '소모전으로 치닫다'.

examples.en: In art class we did a drawing with pencils.
The teacher said that drawing is the foundation of painting.

examples.ko: 그 화가의 소묘 작품이 전시되고 있어요.
examples.en: The painter's sketch works are on display.
I was surprised that the landscape sketch was as accurate as a photo.
I started with a sketch and added color later.

examples.ko: 이 소묘에는 빛과 그림자가 잘 표현돼 있어요.
examples.en: Light and shadow are well expressed in this drawing.

explain: 주로 연필이나 목탄으로 선과 명암을 살려 그린 그림이에요. 일상에서는 '스케치'라고 더 쉽게 말하고, '소묘'는 미술 수업이나 전시 설명에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is a picture drawn mainly with pencil or charcoal, using lines and shading. In daily talk people say '스케치' more easily, while '소묘' often appears in art classes and exhibition descriptions.

examples.en: Snow piled up softly and the road turned white.
She heaped rice onto my plate.
Fallen leaves piled up in the flower bed.
Dust has settled thickly on the desk.

examples.ko: 할머니가 그릇에 쌀을 소복이 퍼 주셨어요.
examples.en: Grandmother scooped a heaping bowl of rice for me.

examples.ko: 아이가 모래를 소복이 모아 산을 만들었어요.
examples.en: The child gathered sand into a little mound to make a mountain.

explain: 눈, 낙엽, 밥, 먼지처럼 무언가가 둥글게 볼록 쌓이거나 담긴 모습에 써요. '수북이'와 비슷하게 쓰는 경우가 많아요. 보통 '쌓이다, 담다, 앉다'와 함께 나와요.
explain_en: It describes things such as snow, leaves, rice or dust piled up or filled in a rounded heap. It is often used much like '수북이'. It usually appears with verbs like '쌓이다', '담다' and '앉다'.

examples.ko: 서점에서 영한 소사전을 한 권 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a small English-Korean dictionary at the bookstore.

examples.ko: 이 소사전은 작아서 가방에 넣고 다니기 좋아요.
examples.en: This pocket dictionary is small, so it's easy to carry in a bag.
This word is listed even in the small dictionary.
A travel mini dictionary is handy to have.
It's hard to find difficult words in a small dictionary.

examples.ko: 소사전 한 권이면 기초 단어는 충분해요.
examples.en: One small dictionary is enough for basic words.

explain: 크기가 작고 단어 수가 적은 사전이에요. 반대로 많은 단어를 실은 큰 사전은 '대사전'이라고 해요. 요즘은 종이 사전보다 앱이나 인터넷 사전을 많이 써서 '사전'이라고만 말하는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It is a dictionary with a small size and fewer entries. The opposite, a large one with many entries, is a '대사전'. These days many people use apps or online dictionaries, so they often just say '사전'.

examples.ko: 코로나 이후 소상인들이 큰 어려움을 겪었어요.
examples.en: Small traders went through great difficulty after COVID.
The government announced support measures for small traders.
I talked with the small traders at the market.

examples.ko: 우리 어머니는 작은 가게를 하는 소상인이에요.
examples.en: My mother is a small trader who runs a little shop.
For small traders, rent is the biggest burden.

examples.ko: 대형 마트가 생기자 소상인의 매출이 줄었어요.
examples.en: Once the big supermarket opened, the small traders' sales dropped.

explain: 작은 규모로 장사하는 사람을 말하고, 뉴스에서는 '소상공인'이라는 말도 자주 나와요. 대기업이나 대형 마트와 비교하는 이야기에서 많이 쓰여요.
explain_en: It refers to people who do business on a small scale, and the news also often uses the word '소상공인'. It is commonly used when comparing with big companies or large supermarkets.
